ai.description: This small viper reaches 40 cm. It is reddish-brown with dark, horseshoe-shaped dorsal blotches and a triangular head. A distinct pale postocular stripe and keeled scales are diagnostic.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Horseshoe Pit-viper is best identified by the distinct, dark, horseshoe-shaped marking on the top of its head, which is absent in other similar Indian *Trimeresurus*.
ai.habitat: The Horseshoe Pit-viper inhabits high-altitude montane evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Horseshoe Pit-viper is primarily nocturnal, often found coiled on low vegetation or rocky outcrops where it waits in ambush for small vertebrate prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trimeresurus strigatus* is ovoviviparous, typically producing a litter of 4–10 young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Trimeresurus strigatus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in high-elevation grasslands and shola forests above 1,000 meters.
